seo.title: Saint Anthony of Padua
seo.description: The life of Saint Anthony of Padua, patron of the parish of Dois Vizinhos: from Lisbon to Padua, his preaching, miracles, devotions and how he came to our town.

hero.lead: Born Fernando in Lisbon, he became Anthony — Franciscan friar, preacher to popes and Doctor of the Church. Eight centuries later he remains one of the world's most beloved saints, and the patron of Dois Vizinhos.

portrait.alt: Painting by Francisco de Zurbarán: Saint Anthony kneeling in a Franciscan habit, hands joined, contemplates the Child Jesus appearing in golden light; at his feet, an open book and white lilies
portrait.caption: Francisco de Zurbarán, “Apparition of the Child Jesus to Saint Anthony of Padua”, c. 1627–1630. São Paulo Museum of Art (MASP). Public domain.

timeline.title: From Lisbon to Padua.
timeline.lead: Saint Anthony lived only 36 years. It was enough time to change his name, his order and his country — and to leave his mark on the history of the Church.

items.title: Fernando is born in Lisbon
items.description: According to tradition, Fernando de Bulhões is born on August 15 into a noble family near Lisbon Cathedral.

items.title: An early religious life
items.description: At 15 he joins the Canons Regular of Saint Augustine. At the Monastery of Santa Cruz in Coimbra he devotes himself to deep study of the Scriptures.

items.title: He becomes a Franciscan
items.description: Moved by the first Franciscan martyrs, killed in Morocco, he exchanges the Augustinian habit for that of Saint Francis and takes the name Anthony.

items.title: Shipwreck and meeting Francis
items.description: He sets out on mission to Africa, falls ill and, on the way back, a storm drives his ship to Sicily. In Assisi he attends the Chapter of Mats alongside Saint Francis.

items.title: The preacher revealed
items.description: In Forlì, asked at the last minute to preach at an ordination, he astonishes everyone with his wisdom. An intense mission across Italy and France begins.

items.title: First teacher of theology
items.description: Saint Francis allows him to teach theology to the friars, provided study does not extinguish the spirit of prayer and devotion.

items.title: “I see my Lord”
items.description: Ill and exhausted, he dies on June 13 at Arcella, near Padua. It is said the city's children ran through the streets crying: the saint is dead.

items.title: A saint in less than a year
items.description: On May 30, Pope Gregory IX canonizes him — one of the fastest canonizations in Church history.

items.title: The incorrupt tongue
items.description: When his remains are transferred, Saint Bonaventure finds the great preacher's tongue intact. The relic is venerated to this day in the Basilica of Padua.

items.title: Doctor of the Church
items.description: Pope Pius XII proclaims him Doctor of the Church, with the title Evangelical Doctor, for the faithfulness and depth of his preaching.

symbols.title: What each detail means.
symbols.lead: Christian art teaches through images. In Zurbarán's canvas, four symbols tell us who Saint Anthony was.

child.title: The Child Jesus
child.description: Recalls the vision the saint had in prayer, when the Child appeared to him. A sign of Anthony's intimacy with Christ.

book.title: The open book
book.description: The Holy Scriptures, which he knew by heart. It recalls the preacher and Doctor of the Church.

lily.title: The lilies
lily.description: A symbol of purity of heart and a life given entirely to God.

habit.title: The Franciscan habit
habit.description: The simple cloth and cord speak of poverty, humility and the choice to follow Jesus like Saint Francis.

devotions.title: How people pray with Saint Anthony.
devotions.lead: Over the centuries, the simple faith of the people created traditions that crossed the ocean and reached us.

novena.title: The Trezena
novena.description: Thirteen days of prayer, from June 1 to 13, prepare for the patron's feast. In Dois Vizinhos it comes together with the parish fair and a big community celebration.

bread.title: Saint Anthony's Bread
bread.description: Inspired by the saint's charity toward the hungry, bread blessed on the 13th reminds us that faith is proven by sharing with the poor.

lost.title: Finder of lost things
lost.description: Tradition says a psalter taken without permission was returned after the saint prayed. Ever since, people ask his help to find what was lost.

marriage.title: The matchmaker saint
marriage.description: Known for helping young people start families, he became the patron of couples in Brazil — and June became the month of festivals and petitions.

town.title: He arrived before the town.
town.lead: In {{arrival}}, the first devotees brought Saint Anthony to a small village in southwestern Paraná. In {{founded}}, the chapel on the main square became a parish — even before Dois Vizinhos was a municipality.
town.quote: Saint Anthony arrived in Dois Vizinhos before the first mayor.
town.quoteSource: Valdir Luiz Pagnoncelli, “History of the 40 years of Saint Anthony of Padua Parish”
town.imageAlt: Altar of the main church of Saint Anthony of Padua, with the great cross beneath the arch

prayer.title: Prayer to Saint Anthony
lines: Glorious Saint Anthony, friend of the poor and preacher of the Gospel,
intercede for our parish and for every family in Dois Vizinhos.
Help us find what we have lost and, above all, never to lose our faith.
Teach us to love the Word of God and to serve others with joy.
